newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch shares closed at a record high on Monday, with a surge in cyclical stocks ahead of results this week livening up an otherwise lacklustre market.

"Outside of the cyclicals it's been pretty dull with volumes only moderately ticking over," said one dealer. "People are looking at stocks like Akzo and DSM which report half year figures and are thinking their PE (price/earnings) multiples are way out of line with some of the growth stocks," he added.
The AEX index closed 3.86 points higher at a record 992.89, back from a session high of 994.82 but inching back towards the 1,006.26 all time high set last Wednesday.
"People are anticipating good half year results from Akzo and DSM and are thinking the shares are looking a little undervalued when you look at the PEs," the dealer added.

He said cyclicals might be expected to have fairly low PEs, reflecting sedate growth patterns compared to faster expanding, more acquisitive firms, but that some had been left behind by the explosion in share prices over the last two years.
"With a PE of around 10 for DSM the stock looks undervalued. When you look at some of the other multiples in the AEX, the cyclicals haven't done nearly as well," he said. Typically,
Dealers said the AEX seemed to be taking a breather after rising around 126 points during July, although investors' appetite for stock did not appear to be blunted long-term.
"If we can close above 1,000 points on the AEX that would be a very bullish signal," said a dealer.
"We believe the market is probably expensive and could use a correction but once we close above 1,000 we wouldn't be surprised to see 1,100 or 1,200 pretty quickly after," he added.
"At these levels, with the way we've come up so much this year and last year you'd have to say a correction of 10 percent or so was a realistic prospect," he said.
